newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: JUPITERS SAYS WELL-PLACED IN GAMING MARKET.
newsitem.headline: JUPITERS SAYS WELL-PLACED IN GAMING MARKET.

text.p: Queensland casino operator Jupiters Ltd said on Friday that the Brisbane casino continues to improve and that with the recently launched statewide Jupiters Keno the company was well-placed in the competitive gaming market.
Jupiters earlier reported a net profit of A$41.29 million for the year to June 30, up from A$33.86 million previously, and lifted its final dividend by a cent to seven cents a share.

The casino and hotel operator said revenue from its Gold Coast operation rose 15 percent to A$306.2 million, although the previous year had been affected by a casino refurbishment and tax differences.
Hotel occupancy esed slightly to 78.1 percent with a flat average room rate due to an oversupply of hotel rooms on the Gold Coast.
In Brisbane, revenues rose 14 percent to A$182.8 million and patronage rose from a daily average of 9,000 to 10,000.
Jupiters said it was increasing marketing after premium player activity was below expectations for most of the year.
Hotel occupancy improved from 34.9 percent to 54.3 percent.
Work to make the casino lighter and more colourful would be completed in March 1998, at a forecast cost of A$16 million.
Jupiters shares were three cents at A$3.31 at 11.00 a.m. (0100 GMT).
